header.subtitle: Store plugins bring in libraries from other stores and install games you own. Each one is a separate program; Platypus only runs the ones you approve.

section.data: data plugins · no code, always on

empty.label: no store plugins
empty.detail: Put a plugin folder in ~/.local/share/platypus/plugins and rescan. From Platypus's source: plugins/install.sh epic-legendary.

card.dataNote: JSON only — fix recipes and tweaks. It can't run anything, so Platypus applies it without asking.

auth.loggedOutHidden: Logged out: its games are hidden
auth.loginStays: Your login stays with {{name}}'s own tool; Platypus doesn't store it.
auth.stepStorePage: 1 · log in on the store's page
auth.stillLoggedOut: The store says you are still logged out.
auth.checkFailing: Login check is failing ({{count}} attempts). Retrying…
auth.checkDead: Login check keeps failing. Close and try again.
auth.actionFailed: Platypus couldn't finish that plugin action.

notify.installsIntoGames: {{name}} installs into the Games folder again
notify.willRetry: {{name}} will start again on the next call

approve.title: Approve {{name}}
approve.changedWarning: Its program changed since you approved it. If you didn't update it yourself, don't approve it.
approve.warning: A store plugin runs with your user's permissions. The hosts and paths above are what it declares; Platypus doesn't enforce them yet. Platypus does check every game it launches is inside the plugin's install folder. Approve plugins you trust.

settings.notApplied: Saved, but the plugin did not take it yet
settings.saveFailed: The plugin couldn't save that setting.
